questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Which vegetables are the healthiest for children
How to cook quick meals after work
Why children today eat more fast food
How parents can make family meals less stressful
questions.why: They hear from experts on how to make dinnertime something everyone enjoys, without conflict.

questions.q: What does Georgie say about the foods she disliked as a child?
options: She now loves them as an adult
She still refuses to eat them
She was allergic to them
Her parents never cooked them
questions.why: She hated nuts and avocados as a child, but now she absolutely loves both.

questions.q: What does Neil say about his own eating as a child?
options: He hated Brussels sprouts
He only ate rice and beans
He liked most foods
He refused to eat vegetables
questions.why: Neil says, 'I think I liked most things.'

questions.q: What does Charlotte Stirling-Reed say about her own children's eating?
options: They always eat everything that she cooks for them
Their appetite changes with weather, activity and mood
They only eat properly when they are with friends
They eat much more in winter than in summer
questions.why: She says their appetite goes up and down, depending on the weather, their day and their mood.

questions.q: Why does Dr Anne Fishel think dinnertime can cause so much tension?
options: Eating is one of the few things kids can control
Parents often cook food that is too spicy
Children are too tired and hungry in the evening
Families eat together too rarely these days
questions.why: She says it's one of the few areas they control: kids decide whether they're going to eat it.

questions.q: Why does Neil say 'imagine how hard it could be' before talking about food allergies?
options: To show that allergies are very rare
To suggest that experts don't understand allergies
To say that allergies make children eat more
To suggest meals are even harder when a child has an allergy
questions.why: He says if experts struggle at mealtimes, a child with a food allergy could make it even harder.

questions.q: What solution did Sharon Wee find for her daughter?
options: Cooking a completely different meal every day
Giving her only fresh fruit and vegetables
Rice and beans, which she ate for about five years
Taking her to a special restaurant each week
questions.why: Sharon says rice and beans was the winning formula, eaten for about the first five years.

questions.q: Which way of giving children a choice do the experts suggest?
options: Letting them cook their own dinner with an adult
Offering small, healthy snacks and dips first
Letting them eat in front of the TV on weekends
Allowing a small dessert before the main meal
questions.why: Neil says one agreed tip is to offer small, healthy snacks and dips before the meal.
